- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ levels), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the magnitude of the correction.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift toward historical averages too quickly, missing the true price’s momentum or volatility.
- Model underestimates downward trends in the latter half of the horizon, particularly when prices are falling below 70.
- Model overestimates volatility in the early days of the forecast window, especially when prices are trending upward.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistent underestimation of price drops after mid-February or during low-demand periods.
- Model shows lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates the depth of the correction until 10–15 days into the forecast.
- Model tends to overfit to recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation when prices are falling from peaks.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy changes or market interventions — e.g., when ETS auction prices drop sharply after regulatory announcements, model doesn’t adjust quickly enough.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — forecasts remain near recent highs even when true prices are falling, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast.
